confirmed_gaps.observed: 1e100 -> 1.0000000000000006e+100 (off by 3 ULP), 1e-100 -> 9.999999999999994e-101. Verified via --emit-llvm: the IR stores 'double 0x54B249AD2594C380' whereas the true 1e100 is 0x54B249AD2594C37D, so the wrong VALUE is baked into the constant -- the repr (py_float_repr_shortest) is faithfully printing a wrong double. llvmlite itself serializes 1e100 correctly (0x...c37d), so the defect is upstream in the parser. 1e16, 1e17, 0.1, 0.1+0.2, 1234567890.123456 are all correct (small enough exponents that the iterative error stays < 0.5 ULP).
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: pcc/frontends/python/py_parse.py:_parse_float_literal (lines 98-121) computes the value by multiplying/dividing a float mantissa by _pow10f(exp), and _pow10f (lines 88-95) builds 10**exp by repeated float multiplication (out = out * 10.0, exp times). Repeated float multiply accumulates rounding error (~1/2 ULP per step), so for exp~100 the result is several ULP off. CPython parses float literals with a correctly-rounded string->double conversion (David Gay / strtod). The hand-rolled parser is used because it must remain self-hostable (pcc1 parsing pcc's own source), and float(<runtime str>) currently forces a libpython fallback, so it cannot simply call float(text). A correctly-rounded, self-host-safe replacement builds the EXACT integer mantissa and scales by an exact power of ten in a SINGLE operation: value = float(mantissa_int * 10**k) for k>=0, else mantissa_int / 10**(-k) (Python int truediv is correctly rounded in CPython). This matched CPython exactly for 1e100/1e-100/1e300/1.5e300/0.1/3.14/1234567890.123456/1e16/1e17/2.675 in a host cross-check. IMPORTANT: this fix DEPENDS on the _to_double bignum fix (the float(bignum) / bignum-truediv finding) landing first -- without it, float(10**100) is 0.0 and 1/(10**100) raises under pcc1, so the new parser would be wrong under self-host. Apply that edit first, then this one.

Requires the _to_double bignum fix (float(bignum) and bignum truediv) to be landed FIRST or pcc1 self-host will mis-parse large-exponent literals. _pow10f and _pow10 may become unused after this (and a sibling that may also call _pow10f) -- grep before removing them.
